intended_object: The conjugation action morphism U ×_K U_r → U_r, (g, s) ↦ g s g⁻¹. Here U is the unitriangular group scheme over a commutative ring K and U_r is its closed normal r-th superdiagonal stage. I inferred this from the docstring, the module documentation and its use as the witness for IsMonHom.Normal.
explanation: The body identifies U ×_K U_r with Spec of the tensor product of the coordinate rings. It takes the two universal points g and s, turns them into matrices u ∈ U(R) and v ∈ U_r(R), forms u v u⁻¹, and maps this point back to a morphism into U_r. The point lies in the superdiagonal subgroup because that matrix subgroup is normal. This is the standard Yoneda construction of conjugation from the universal point. The lemma unitriangularStageConjugation_inclusion proves that the map, composed with the closed immersion, equals (U ◁ ι) ≫ GrpObj.conj U. The immersion is a monomorphism, so this property determines the map uniquely, and the definition is exactly the restricted conjugation G × N → N. It works for every commutative base ring K and all n and r, degenerate cases included. Mathlib has only the unrestricted conjugation GrpObj.conj and the existence-only class IsMonHom.Normal, so this specific object is stated at its natural generality.
